title: Using the A Minor Pentatonic Scale Across All Five Positions

objectives: Identify the five notes of the minor pentatonic scale in any key
Play all five positions cleanly at a moderate tempo
Transition between adjacent positions without pausing
Improvise using the scale in a musical context
prerequisites: Can play a one-octave major scale
Knows the note names on the low E string up to the 12th fret
metadata.prompt: create a lesson on how to use the minor pentatonic scale and the various positions

sections.title: What the minor pentatonic scale is
sections.body: The A minor pentatonic scale uses five notes derived from the A natural minor scale, omitting the 2nd and 6th degrees. This produces a stable, blues-friendly sound with no semitone clashes between adjacent scale tones. In A minor the five notes are A / C / D / E / G, corresponding to the intervals root (1), minor third (b3), perfect fourth (4), perfect fifth (5), and minor seventh (b7). On the fretboard it is usually taught as five overlapping positions; learning to move between them smoothly is the foundation for improvising solos.

sections.title: Position 1: A minor pentatonic, frets 5-8
sections.body: Position 1 covers frets 5 through 8 and contains every note of the scale in a compact span. Play it ascending and descending, using one finger per fret where possible, and keep your thumb behind the neck. Once you can play it cleanly at a moderate tempo, connect it to position 2 by shifting to the nearest shared note on the same string rather than jumping.

sections.title: Position 5: A minor pentatonic, frets 14-17
sections.body: Position 5 covers frets 14 through 17 and contains every note of the scale in a compact span. Play it ascending and descending, using one finger per fret where possible, and keep your thumb behind the neck. Once you can play it cleanly at a moderate tempo, return toward position 4 through the shared high-E note at fret 15 (play frets 17, 15, 12 descending).

practice_steps.goal: Memorize position 1 shape and play it cleanly
practice_steps.action: Play the A minor pentatonic position 1 (frets 5-8) up and down at 60 BPM, one note per click, using alternate picking. Start on the root on the low E string (string 6, fret 5), ascend the full box to fret 8 on the high E string, then descend back to fret 5 on string 6. Add a slight accent on each marked root note (blue circles with R).
practice_steps.success_criterion: You can ascend to fret 8 and descend back to fret 5 twice in a row without stopping or missing a note.

practice_steps.action: On string 1 (high E), play eight quarter notes in two bars of 4/4: frets 5, 8, 10, 8 | 8, 10, 8, 5. Fret 8 is shared by positions 1 and 2; fret 10 enters position 2, and the final fret 5 returns to A.
practice_steps.success_criterion: You can play the full two-bar phrase without stopping and end cleanly on fret 5 (the root A).

practice_steps.goal: Connect all five positions along one string
practice_steps.action: Start on the root of position 1 on string 6 (fret 5) and play the pentatonic notes ascending along string 6 through position 5, then reverse and descend: frets 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 15, 12, 10, 8, 5 — one note per click, no stopping. This connects all five boxes along one string; do not attempt to jump back from position 5 to position 1 — they sit an octave apart.
practice_steps.success_criterion: One unbroken ascending and descending pass through all five positions along string 6.

practice_steps.action: Over an A minor backing track, improvise for two minutes using only position 1. Emphasize the root and the minor third. Rest for the same amount of time between takes.
practice_steps.success_criterion: You can improvise for the full two minutes without playing outside the scale.

practice_steps.action: Improvise over the same backing track, but now deliberately move between positions every four bars. Target the root note in each new position as your landing note.
practice_steps.success_criterion: You land on the root in at least three different positions across the take.

tips: Think of the five positions as one connected shape on the fretboard, not five separate patterns — every position shares notes with its neighbours.
Anchor your hand with your index finger at the low end of each position; this keeps your other three fingers free for the higher frets.
Practice positions in reverse order (5 back to 1) occasionally — most players over-rely on positions 1 and 2.
Sing the root note before you start improvising so your ear has a target, not just your fingers.
